newsitem.title: GERMANY: BT/MCI's Concert venture to double revs in 1997.
newsitem.headline: BT/MCI's Concert venture to double revs in 1997.

text.p: Concert, the global telecoms venture of British Telecommunications and MCI, confirmed on Thursday that it expected revenues to double in 1997, a senior BT executive said.
"Concert revenues will approach $1 billion this year," BT global communications director Alfred Mockett told Reuters.
Concert, which aims to serve multinational customers globally end-to-end, is expected to break into profit at the operating level within the next 18 months.
BT officials rejected comparisons with Global One, a competing alliance, made this week by Deutsche Telekom chairman Ron Sommer.
Sommer said the Global One alliance of France Telecom, Deutsche Telekom and Sprint Corp had around 30,000 customers and was about twice the size of Concert on an "apples to apples comparison".
"He's not comparing apples to apples," said Mockett, adding that he believed that Global One includes revenues from its parents whereas Concert does not.
BT says Concert has about 35,000 business customers, the bulk being existing customers, from either BT or MCI, which are taking new services.
"Compared to Global One and Unisource (another global rival), Concert looks terrific," BT's finance director Robert Brace told reporters in London.

Any comparison between global alliances is difficult because of the different structures of the companies and the complexities of combining their individual business accounts that make up their clientel of multinational companies.
